title: zazzle-csharp-indexer limitations
description: Limits of the tool as a whole. Limits of its parts are in the limitations.json of src/Index, src/Analysis, src/Tools, src/View, src/Mcp and src/Cli. The README's Known limits section stays the reader's list.

entities.title: macOS first, Linux second, Windows untested
entities.summary: macOS is the primary target and Linux is built and tested; Windows is untested.
entities.impact: Releases build osx-arm64, osx-x64, linux-x64 and linux-arm64 only. Some code paths already step aside on Windows (realpath, socket permissions, spawning the daemon), but nothing checks that they work there.

sources.symbol: Build the C# indexer for both CPU types

entities.title: A large, unsigned binary
entities.summary: The published file is large (self-contained, with Roslyn, ReadyToRun, untrimmed) and is not Developer ID signed: the release signs the other tools when signing is configured, but not the indexer.
entities.impact: A big file per platform; the release gzips the macOS ones.
entities.workaround: Install it with the zazzle Homebrew formula: Homebrew does not quarantine what a formula installs, so it runs without a Gatekeeper prompt.

entities.title: Builds outside a release all say 0.0.0-dev
entities.summary: Only the release workflow passes a version to the build, so every local or CI build reports 0.0.0-dev, and the daemon handshake sees two such builds as the same version.
entities.impact: A daemon started by one development build keeps serving serve and zazzled clients of a newer development build until it is idle for the idle period; the new code is not used meanwhile. A release build and a development build differ, so either replaces an idle daemon of the other.
entities.workaround: End the running daemon process before trying a development build. serve --no-daemon (ZAZZLE_INDEXER_NO_DAEMON=1) avoids the daemon for MCP sessions, but zazzled always goes through it.
